title: Travels to New York and Boston
summary: Williams describes his first trip out in 1926 to New York, a quick Boston visit, and hearing bands on Broadway including Louis Prima.

blocks.x: You ever hear any music in Omaha?
No, I never been there. You kind of think that you mentioned that.
They have some guys up there that spoke to that pretty good brass. Yeah. I never been to Omaha. No. I want to, I could have went to Omaha without paying out from Chicago.

See, I got a pass there to go to Chicago every time I want. But out of Chicago, going to Omaha, Nebraska, on the Chicago Northwestern Railroad, I could ride from there without any pay. And Union Pacific, out of Omaha, Nebraska, half back. So I didn't go.
Did you make many trips when you first came to New Orleans? Did you get out much out of the city?

Well, I started getting out here in 1926. My first trip going out of here is going to New York. And I got off the train, a little above Atlanta, Georgia. I walked a couple miles. Finally, I got the right train. I went home. When I get to Washington, D.C., I had to pay half a pass from Washington to New York. Well, since then, I was with the railroad over, you had to be with the railroad over eight years to get a pass all the way through. So after that, I started going from place to place. I went to Boston about three years ago. I left New York and went to Boston.
Bet you heard some good bands all over the country.

Well, I didn't get much out of Boston. I'll tell you, I only stayed there about six hours. I came on back to New York. New York is a town where you hear plenty of music, plenty of music. Get on Broadway, Broadway, and 52nd, you hear all kinds of bands playing up there. I didn't get nothing much out of Portland, Oregon.
What kind of bands did you listen to in New York? Jazz band?
I just wondered if you remember any of the guys' names.

Well, no, I didn't know none of whom they were. But once, in 51, I believe, the time when Lewis and the other Lewis was playing, one was playing 48 and by the way, the other was playing 49. Lewis, what's his name? Italian boy, what's his name? Lewis, Lewis. Prima? Yeah. They both was playing on Broadway the same time. Oh, wow. Mm-hmm. Louis Prima. Did you ever go to Chicago and hear many bands there?
